people.name: The Game
people.description: American rapper Jayceon Terrell Taylor, known as The Game, reached No. 1 in the US in 2005 with his debut album, The Documentary. The 2006 follow-up, Doctor's Advocate, achieved double platinum certification and earned two Grammy Award nominations for its single 'Hate It or Love It' (featuring 50 Cent), in the categories of Best Rap Song and Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. In 2011, entry to Canada was refused to Game due to alleged Los Angeles gang ties, with concert organisers stating he was associated with the Bloods, an African American street gang.

people.name: Apl.De.Ap
people.description: Filipino-American rapper, singer and record producer Apl.De.Ap achieved a US and UK No.1 single in 2003 titled 'Where Is The Love' with the Black Eyed Peas. Later in 2008, he established the Apl Foundation International (Aplfi) to support children and various communities across the Philippines and Asia.

people.name: Keith Carlock
people.description: American musician Keith Carlock has provided drum performances for Toto, Steely Dan, James Taylor, John Mayer, and Sting. During the 2009 Modern Drummer Readers Poll, he received the title of best Pop, Fusion, and All-Around drummer.

people.name: Martin Carr
people.description: Martin Carr, guitarist, singer with English alternative rock band The Boo Radleys, who had the 1995 UK No.9 single 'Wake Up Boo'. Their name is taken from the character Boo Radley in Harper Lee's 1960 novel, To Kill a Mockingbird. After the breakup of the Boo Radleys, Carr launched a solo career, taking the name bravecaptain from a song by the US rock band Firehose.

people.name: Jonathan Knight
people.description: Jonathan Knight is a member of the American boy band New Kids on the Block. The group scored a UK No.1 single in 1989 with 'You Got It, The Right Stuff' and a US No.1 single in 1990 with 'Step By Step'. Achieving success throughout the late 1980s and early 1990s, they have worldwide record sales exceeding 80 million.

people.name: Wendy Wu
people.description: Wendy Wu belonged to the English new wave band the Photos, which achieved a top 5 album on the UK Albums Chart in 1980. Afterward, Wu put out a few solo singles across 1982 and 1983, before partnering with Steve Strange in 1986 to create the duo Strange Cruise.

people.name: Michael Dempsey
people.description: Michael Dempsey is the bassist for the English new wave group The Lotus Eaters, known for their 1983 UK No. 15 single 'First Picture Of You', which also charted successfully across continental Europe, particularly in France, Italy, Belgium, and Spain. Additionally, Dempsey has collaborated with The Cure and Associates.

people.name: Jennifer Batten
people.description: Jennifer Batten is an American guitarist whose career includes work as a solo artist and session musician. She performed during all three world tours undertaken by Michael Jackson, and she subsequently spent the years 1999 to 2001 recording and touring alongside Jeff Beck.

people.name: Chris Bailey
people.description: Chris Bailey was an Australian singer, songwriter, musician, and producer, as well as the co-founder and vocalist of the rock group the Saints. Their 1976 debut single, '(I'm) Stranded', has been described as "one of the iconic singles of the era" and came out before the first releases from contemporary punk groups like the Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, and The Clash. Australian Musician magazine named it the fourth most important moment in Australian pop and rock history in 2007. Bailey passed away on 9 April 2022 at the age of 65.

people.name: Barry Goudreau
people.description: Barry Goudreau played guitar for Boston, whose work includes the 1977 UK No.22 single 'More Than A Feeling' and the 1986 US No.1 single 'Amanda'. As one of the world's best-selling artists, Boston have achieved worldwide sales of more than 75 million records, which includes 31 million albums in the United States. Within the US total, their self-titled debut album accounted for 17 million copies and their second album, Don't Look Back, accounted for seven million.

people.name: Roger Troutman
people.description: Roger Troutman was an American composer, songwriter, producer, multi-instrumentalist and the founder of the band Zapp who helped spearhead the funk movement and heavily influenced west coast hip hop due to the scene's heavy sampling of his music over the years. Troutman was found shot and critically wounded outside his northwest Dayton recording studio on 25th April 1999.

people.name: Ronnie Montrose
people.description: American musician and guitarist Ronnie Montrose played in the band Montrose, whose 1973 debut album has often been cited as "America's answer to Led Zeppelin", and the Edgar Winter Group, which released the 1973 single 'Frankenstein' that reached No. 1 in the US and No. 18 in the UK. Alongside his work as a session musician with numerous other artists, he died at the age of 64 on 3 March 2012 from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after taking his own life.

people.name: Felix Cavaliere
people.description: Felix Cavaliere played keyboards for the American rock band The Rascals, which was initially known as The Young Rascals. The group achieved US No.1 hits with the songs 'Good Lovin'' in 1966, 'Groovin'' in 1967, and 'People Got to Be Free' in 1968.

people.name: Twink
people.description: Twink (John Alder) is an English drummer, singer, songwriter, and a key figure in the English psychedelic movement who played in The Pretty Things and The Pink Fairies. In 1967, Twink recorded as part of Santa Barbara Machine Head alongside Ronnie Wood, Kim Gardner, who later joined Ashton, Gardner & Dyke, and keyboardist Jon Lord, who subsequently joined Deep Purple. Later on, Twink converted to Islam and took the name Mohammed Abdullah.

people.name: Tim Davis
people.description: Tim Davis was an American drummer, singer, songwriter, and co-founder of the Steve Miller Band. The band achieved the 1974 US No.1 and 1990 UK No.1 single 'The Joker', the 1976 hit 'Fly Like an Eagle', and the 1982 US No.1 hit 'Abracadabra'. He passed away on September 20, 1988, at the age of 44.

people.name: Jody Miller
people.description: American singer Jody Miller achieved commercial success across the country, folk, and pop genres. Her 1965 song 'Queen of the House', created as an answer song to Roger Miller's 'King of the Road', led to her becoming the second female artist to win a country music accolade from the Grammy Awards. Miller passed away on October 6, 2022, at the age of 80.

people.name: Denny Doherty
people.description: Denny Doherty was a member of the American folk rock vocal group The Mamas & the Papas, known for the 1965 hit 'California Dreamin'', the 1966 US No.1 single 'Monday Monday', and the 1967 hit 'Dedicated to the One I Love'. Following a short illness, Doherty passed away on 19th Jan 2007 at the age of 66. His musical career began in 1956 as part of a band named the Hepsters, and he later formed a friendship in 1963 with Cass Elliot during her time with The Big 3.

people.name: Chuck Mangione
people.description: American flugelhorn player, trumpeter and composer Chuck Mangione, whose single 'Feels So Good' reached No.4 in the US in 1978, passed away in his sleep at his home in Rochester on July 22, 2025, at the age of 84.

people.name: Meco Monardo
people.description: American record producer and musician, Meco Monardo, who had the 1977 US No.1 & UK No.7 single 'Star Wars Theme'. As a session musician, he played the trombone with acts like Diana Ross. He performed on Diana Ross' 1980 album Diana as a favour to producer (and neighbour) Nile Rodgers. His solo on the single 'I'm Coming Out' is notable because of the rarity of trombone features on post-big-band era pop records.

people.name: John Mayall
people.description: John Mayall was an English blues and rock musician, songwriter, and producer, known as the 'father of the UK blues movement'. His Bluesbreakers Band featured Eric Clapton, Mick Taylor, Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Jack Bruce, Peter Green, and Jimmy McCulloch. His career spanned nearly seven decades, and he remained an active musician until his death. Mayall passed away at his California home on 22 July 2024 at the age of 90.

people.name: Merle Travis
people.description: Country singer and songwriter Merle Travis gained renown for his distinct guitar playing, a technique still called Travis picking within the guitar community. Among his songwriting credits is 'Sixteen Tons', which became a US No.1 hit for Ernie Ford in 1955. His career honors include an induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1970 and election to the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1977. Travis passed away from a heart attack at his residence in Tahlequah, Oklahoma, on 20th October 1983.

works.title: GNX
works.eventDescription: Kendrick Lamar secured the No. 1 spot on the UK chart with his sixth studio album, GNX, marking his second chart-topper in the region following 2015's To Pimp a Butterfly. On the global Spotify chart, GNX pulled in more than 44.2 million streams on its first day, averaging over 3.6 million per track even though it was released only seven hours beforehand. Domestically, the album entered the Billboard 200 at No. 1 with 319,000 album-equivalent units, backed by 379.72 million official on-demand streams.

works.title: Calypso
works.eventDescription: American musician and songwriter Irving Burgie, considered among the greatest composers of Caribbean music, passed away at the age of 95. He wrote 34 tracks for Harry Belafonte, which included eight out of the 11 tracks featured on the 1956 Belafonte album Calypso, marking the initial record of any sort to reach one million in sales. In 2007, he became an inductee of the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

works.title: Dirty Water
works.eventDescription: Dick Dodd, who served as the drummer and singer for The Standells on their 1966 hit song 'Dirty Water', passed away from cancer at age 68. The track grew into an anthem for sports fans in Boston because of its refrain "Boston, you're my home," even though the band possessed no direct ties to the city.

works.title: I Dreamed a Dream
works.eventDescription: Susan Boyle achieved a No.1 position on the UK chart with her album, marking the best-selling debut in UK chart history. The 48 year-old runner-up in ITV's Britain's Got Talent sold 410,000 copies of 'I Dreamed a Dream'. Additionally, Boyle reached the top of the US charts, establishing a first-week sales record for a female debut album after selling 701,000 copies in its opening week.

works.title: Taxman
works.eventDescription: Beatles guitarist George Harrison died in Los Angeles of lung cancer aged 58. Following the breakup of The Beatles Harrison had a successful career as a solo artist and later as part of the Traveling Wilburys. The youngest member of The Beatles, (aged 16 when he joined), his compositions include ‘Taxman’, ‘Here Comes the Sun’, ‘Something’, and ‘While My Guitar Gently Weeps’. Harrison released the acclaimed triple album, All Things Must Pass, in 1970, from which came the worldwide No.1 single 'My Sweet Lord.'

works.title: Perfect Day
works.eventDescription: A collaborative version of "Perfect Day" featuring 29 major artists, among them Elton John, Bono, Tom Jones, and David Bowie, claimed the No. 1 spot on the UK singles chart as a fundraising single for the BBC Children In Need charity. The track was initially composed and recorded in 1973 by Lou Reed.

works.title: You Give Love a Bad Name
works.eventDescription: Bon Jovi achieved their initial major hit in the US when "You Give Love A Bad Name" claimed the No.1 spot. The track was co-authored by band leaders Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora alongside Desmond Child, a songwriter recognized for his contributions to "I Was Made For Lovin' You" by Kiss and "Dude (Looks Like A Lady)" by Aerosmith. The subsequent single by Bon Jovi, "Livin' On A Prayer," was crafted by this same three-person songwriting team.

works.title: You Can’t Hurry Love
works.eventDescription: Originally launched in the UK to anthologise contemporary chart hits, the Now That's What I Call Music series derived its name from a 1930s Danish bacon advertising poster depicting a pig listening to a singing chicken and saying, "Now, That's What I Call Music." The initial volume featured You Can't Hurry Love by Phil Collins as its opening track, alongside popular songs such as 'Karma Chameleon', 'Red Red Wine', and 'Total Eclipse Of The Heart'. Volume 44 from 1999 stands as the most successful installment and the largest-selling compilation album in history, moving 2.3 million copies and beginning with Britney Spears' ...Baby One More Time.

works.title: Double Fantasy
works.eventDescription: The album Double Fantasy by John and Yoko was released in 1980. Despite initial poor reception, the album became notable for its association with Lennon's murder three weeks after its release. Following this event, the record achieved worldwide commercial success and subsequently won Album of the Year at the 24th Annual Grammy Awards in 1981.

works.title: Super Trouper
works.eventDescription: ABBA achieved their final and ninth No.1 single in the UK with "Super Trouper", marking the band's 25th Top 40 hit in the country. The title "Super Trouper" came from the large spotlights utilized during stadium performances.

works.title: Like a Hurricane
works.eventDescription: At the Broken Arrow Ranch located in Woodside, California, Neil Young tracked the song 'Like a Hurricane'. Several years afterward, the track came out on the album American Stars 'n Bars. Throughout the rest of Young's career, the track has stayed a concert staple and a favorite among fans.

works.title: Come Together / Something
works.eventDescription: The Beatles achieved their twenty-sixth US single release and eighteenth US No.1 with 'Come Together / Something', which reached the top of the US singles chart. Lennon drew inspiration for the track from Timothy Leary's gubernatorial campaign against Ronald Reagan in California, which used the slogan "Come together, join the party". ’Something’ marked the initial instance where a composition by George Harrison served as an A-side for the group.

works.title: King of the Road
works.eventDescription: American singer Jody Miller achieved commercial success across the country, folk, and pop genres. Her 1965 song 'Queen of the House', created as an answer song to Roger Miller's 'King of the Road', led to her becoming the second female artist to win a country music accolade from the Grammy Awards. Miller passed away on October 6, 2022, at the age of 80.

works.title: California Dreamin'
works.eventDescription: Denny Doherty was a member of the American folk rock vocal group The Mamas & the Papas, known for the 1965 hit 'California Dreamin'', the 1966 US No.1 single 'Monday Monday', and the 1967 hit 'Dedicated to the One I Love'. Following a short illness, Doherty passed away on 19th Jan 2007 at the age of 66. His musical career began in 1956 as part of a band named the Hepsters, and he later formed a friendship in 1963 with Cass Elliot during her time with The Big 3.

works.title: Feels So Good
works.eventDescription: American flugelhorn player, trumpeter and composer Chuck Mangione, whose single 'Feels So Good' reached No.4 in the US in 1978, passed away in his sleep at his home in Rochester on July 22, 2025, at the age of 84.

works.title: Star Wars Theme
works.eventDescription: American record producer and musician, Meco Monardo, who had the 1977 US No.1 & UK No.7 single 'Star Wars Theme'. As a session musician, he played the trombone with acts like Diana Ross. He performed on Diana Ross' 1980 album Diana as a favour to producer (and neighbour) Nile Rodgers. His solo on the single 'I'm Coming Out' is notable because of the rarity of trombone features on post-big-band era pop records.

works.title: Sixteen Tons
works.eventDescription: Country singer and songwriter Merle Travis gained renown for his distinct guitar playing, a technique still called Travis picking within the guitar community. Among his songwriting credits is 'Sixteen Tons', which became a US No.1 hit for Ernie Ford in 1955. His career honors include an induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1970 and election to the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1977. Travis passed away from a heart attack at his residence in Tahlequah, Oklahoma, on 20th October 1983.
